task: T72 isolated source-level allocation bounds oracle

vulnerable_revision.read_guard: CheckReadLength(static_cast<size_t>(arrayLength), BYTE_SIZE_32), BYTE_SIZE_32=4; the helper accepts when count <= remaining bytes and count*4 <= remaining bytes.
writes: type[i] writes 4 bytes for each i in [0,count)
id[i] writes 8 bytes for each i in [0,count)
vulnerable_revision.conclusion: The guard bounds serialized input bytes but does not scale destination allocations by element size. For any accepted positive count N, requested sizes are N and N bytes while loops write 4N and 8N bytes respectively. Aggregate excess is 3N and 7N bytes.

fixed_revision.other_change: The loop checks a null ReadRemoteObject result before dereferencing it.
fixed_revision.conclusion: Correctly sized allocations match the two indexed write widths.

preconditions_and_counts.guard_acceptance: arrayLength N > 0 and remaining parcel data >= max(N, 4N), which is 4N for positive N. The oracle uses remaining=4N as a source-level accepted boundary; actual Parcel accounting/object encoding is not emulated.

type_array.count_1: 1-byte allocation then 4-byte element-0 store: 3 bytes beyond requested size.
type_array.count_8: 8-byte allocation then 32 bytes of stores: 24 bytes beyond requested size; ASan reports the first OOB at element index 2.

id_array.count_1: 1-byte allocation then 8-byte element-0 store: 7 bytes beyond requested size.
id_array.count_8: 8-byte allocation then 64 bytes of stores: 56 bytes beyond requested size; ASan reports the first OOB at element index 1.

preconditions_and_counts.deduplication: The type[] and id[] writes are two manifestations of one root cause in one function: element-count allocation used as byte count for typed arrays. Count one CVE/root case, not two findings or independent positives.

oracle.build: WSL Debian clang++ 21.1.8; clang++ -std=c++17 -O0 -g -fsanitize=address -fno-omit-frame-pointer oracle.cpp -o oracle
oracle.controls: The harness mirrors only the allocation expressions, bounds guard precondition and typed indexed stores. It does not compile the OpenHarmony function or its dependencies.

interpretation.source_level_result: The exact vulnerable allocation/write width pattern produces heap-buffer-overflow under ASan when the serialized-length guard accepts; the fixed allocation-size expressions pass the same synthetic writes.
interpretation.official_vulnerability_label: CVE-2025-26474 official bulletin identifies communication_ipc improper input validation and restricted-scenario local information disclosure; this oracle corroborates only the memory overwrite mechanism, not disclosure or exploitability.
interpretation.independence_limit: A synthetic harness is a source-level mechanism proof, not a product binary test, Binder route test, scanner prediction, or holdout score. It does not validate the real Parcel byte accounting or attacker reachability.

missing_evidence: Compile and exercise the pinned full component/function with its authentic dependencies and ASan-compatible build profile.
Establish the product route from an attacker-controlled local parcel to the CJ FFI function and exact product build inclusion.
Establish actual parcel byte accounting for serialized remote objects and reproduce against the supported product configuration.
Any detector-scored holdout needs a frozen detector identity and a locked prediction record; none was produced here.
